    def test_bootloader_command_shuts_down_then_enters_bootsel(board: "Board", request: pytest.FixtureRequest, result_note: "Callable[[str], None]") -> None:
        save_fram_raw(board, "bootloader")
        try:
            output = board.run_isolated_expect_reset(DEVICE_SCRIPTS_DIR / "system_command_reboot.py", timeout_s=_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_S, COMMAND="bootloader", STATE="idle")
            facts = _reset_facts(output, parse_facts(output, allow_missing_done=True), "system_command_reboot.py", "bootloader")
            steps = [next((n for n, line in enumerate(output.splitlines()) if step in line), -1) for step in _STEP_LINES]
            assert -1 not in steps and steps == sorted(steps), f"the shutdown's step lines are missing or out of order ({steps}):\n{output}"
            reset = facts.get("reset")
            # No code of its own: the record keeps its acceptance's 9, which BOOTSEL then loses.
            assert isinstance(reset, dict) and reset.get("code") == _RR_COMMAND_INCOMPLETE, f"the bootloader command armed {reset}: {facts}"
            result_note(f"bootloader: {reset}")
            if request.config.getoption("--twin"):
                return
            # picotool answers only a BOOTSEL device: its reboot proves the bootloader was entered; no load, no flash write.
            reboot = subprocess.run(["sudo", "picotool", "reboot"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=_PICOTOOL_TIMEOUT_S, check=False)  # sudo and picotool from the bench host's PATH
            if reboot.returncode != 0:

            reset = facts.get("reset")

    def wait_until(
        check_fn: "Callable[[], bool]",
        timeout_s: float,
        poll_interval_s: float = _WAIT_UNTIL_POLL_S,
        description: str = "condition",
    ) -> bool:
        # Bounded poll-until-condition wait, test-harness-only (never used to change src/'s own real
        # timing - SPECIFICATION.md Part F.3). Polls `check_fn()` until truthy or `timeout_s` elapses,
        # treating a raising check as not-yet-ready; always returns True or raises TimeoutError.
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_s
        last_exc: BaseException | None = None
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            try:
                if check_fn():
                    return True
            except Exception as exc:
                last_exc = exc
            time.sleep(min(poll_interval_s, max(deadline - time.monotonic(), 0.0)))
        try:
            if check_fn():
                return True
        except Exception as exc:
            last_exc = exc
        detail = f" (last error: {last_exc!r})" if last_exc is not None else ""
>       raise TimeoutError(f"timed out after {timeout_s}s waiting for: {description}{detail}")

    def wait_until(
        check_fn: "Callable[[], bool]",
        timeout_s: float,
        poll_interval_s: float = _WAIT_UNTIL_POLL_S,
        description: str = "condition",
    ) -> bool:
        # Bounded poll-until-condition wait, test-harness-only (never used to change src/'s own real
        # timing - SPECIFICATION.md Part F.3). Polls `check_fn()` until truthy or `timeout_s` elapses,
        # treating a raising check as not-yet-ready; always returns True or raises TimeoutError.
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_s
        last_exc: BaseException | None = None
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            try:
                if check_fn():
                    return True
            except Exception as exc:
                last_exc = exc
            time.sleep(min(poll_interval_s, max(deadline - time.monotonic(), 0.0)))
        try:
            if check_fn():
                return True
        except Exception as exc:
            last_exc = exc
        detail = f" (last error: {last_exc!r})" if last_exc is not None else ""

    def test_a_multi_chunk_set_echoes_intact_under_serving_load(board: "Board", bench: "BenchBridge", dut_ip: str) -> None:
        # The serving board's own initiator SETs and GETs a three-chunk echo while the host loads its API: every echo intact,
        # the exerciser's own transfers failing none meanwhile, and the readers answered.
        load = _load.Load()
        stop = threading.Event()
        driver = threading.Thread(target=_echo_load, args=(dut_ip, stop, load), name="echo-load")
        try:
            driver.start()
            output = board.run_isolated(DEVICE_SCRIPTS_DIR / "uart_link_echo_under_serving_load.py", timeout_s=_ECHO_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_S)
        finally:
            stop.set()
            alive = _load.join([driver], 2 * _JOIN_TIMEOUT_S)  # the readers' own bounded join runs inside it
            restore_board_to_serving(board, bench, dut_ip)
        assert not alive, f"{alive} still running after the echo test - it would load every test that follows"
        facts = parse_facts(output)
        assert facts.get("initiator_found") is True, f"the script found no initiating uart_link instance - {_TOML_HINT}: {facts}"
        assert facts.get("load_seen") is True, f"the host's load never reached the script's webserver, so nothing ran under load: {facts}"
        total = facts.get("total")
        assert isinstance(total, int) and total > 0 and facts.get("intact") == total, f"echoes came back damaged or missing under load: {facts}"
        before, after = facts.get("before"), facts.get("after")

    def check_hazard_run_under_load(dut_ip: str, reason: str) -> None:
        # PUT /status's dispatch-only UartHazards starts one run while readers GET /status until it ends: every verdict as
        # the twin judges it, every read answered, the echo resumed with no failure counted, no webserver error and no task ended.

        runs = _hazard_report(dut_ip).get("Runs")
        assert isinstance(runs, int), f"the hazard report counts no runs: {runs!r}"
        before = _link_counters(dut_ip)
        load = _load.Load()
        stop = threading.Event()
        threads = [threading.Thread(target=_gets_until, args=(dut_ip, "/status", n, stop, load), name=f"hazard-get-{n}") for n in range(_ECHO_READERS)]

        finally:
            stop.set()
            alive = _load.join(threads, _JOIN_TIMEOUT_S)

    @pytest.mark.provokes_log(
        "the blocked NTP port's NTP_NO_REPLY the test waits for, and the ceiling's reject-when-full under the readers",
        ("NTP", "E", "NTP_NO_REPLY"),
        ("WEBSERVER", "W", "HTTP_REFUSED"),
        ("WEBSERVER", "W", "HTTP_PEER_RESET"),
    )
    def test_concurrent_get_sensors_under_real_multi_client_load_survives_an_ntp_transient_outage_and_retry(board: Board, bench: "BenchBridge", dut_ip: str, request: pytest.FixtureRequest, result_note: "_load.Note") -> None:
        # A synced client attempts nothing for NTPInterval hours and an unchanged NTPHost PUT fires no post function
        # (src/asy_api_response.py), so the reset under the block makes the boot's first sync fail; the client's own
        # unsynced retry timer then runs inside the block, which lasts one retry period plus a margin.
        networking = _load.get_object(dut_ip, "/networking", _PROBE_TIMEOUT_S)
        res = http_client.fetch(dut_ip, 80, "PUT", "/networking", {"NTPHost": networking.get("NTPHost")}, timeout_s=_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S)
        word = _load.as_object(res.json().get("result"), "result").get("NTPHost")
        assert res.status_code == 200 and word == "Unchanged", f"an NTPHost PUT of its current value answered {word!r}: something was written ({res.body!r})"
        reset_all_error_logs(dut_ip, request.node.name)
        context = " during the NTP outage"
        load = _load.Load(context)
        block_s = _load.ntp_retry_period_s() + _NTP_BLOCK_MARGIN_S
        bench.block_udp_ports([123])
        try:
            _load.reset_and_wait(board, bench, dut_ip, timeout_s=_REBOOT_READY_TIMEOUT_S)
            blocked_until = time.monotonic() + block_s
            resets = threading.Thread(target=_sgp40_resets, args=(dut_ip, load, _DEGRADED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S, context), name="sgp40-resets")
            with _load.readers(_GET_WORKERS, dut_ip, load, iterations=_GET_ITERATIONS_PER_WORKER, timeout_s=_DEGRADED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S, join_s=_DEGRADED_JOIN_TIMEOUT_S, fetch=fetch, others=(resets,)) as alive:
                wait_until(lambda: _load._ntp_error_log_contains(dut_ip, code("E", "NTP_NO_REPLY")), timeout_s=block_s, poll_interval_s=_NTP_RESYNC_POLL_S, description="an NTP attempt meeting the block (NTP_NO_REPLY)")
                time.sleep(max(blocked_until - time.monotonic(), 0.0))
        finally:
            bench.unblock_udp_ports([123])
        assert not alive, f"{alive} never finished within {_DEGRADED_JOIN_TIMEOUT_S:g}s during the NTP outage - possible real deadlock, not just slow requests"
        _assert_load(load, _NTP_MIN_ANSWERED, context, transport_failures_allowed=True)
    
        # The client's own retry timer resyncs once the block lifts: no reset after the one that started the window.
        started = time.monotonic()
        wait_until(lambda: _load.ntp_synced(dut_ip), timeout_s=_NTP_RESYNC_TIMEOUT_S + block_s, poll_interval_s=_NTP_RESYNC_POLL_S, description="NTP resynced by its own retry timer after the block, under bus load")
        result_note(f"NTP resynced {time.monotonic() - started:.1f}s after the block lifted")

    def check_hazard_run_under_load(dut_ip: str, reason: str) -> None:
        # PUT /status's dispatch-only UartHazards starts one run while readers GET /status until it ends: every verdict as
        # the twin judges it, every read answered, the echo resumed with no failure counted, no webserver error and no task ended.
        _require_uart_modules(dut_ip)
        reset_all_error_logs(dut_ip, reason)
        runs = _hazard_report(dut_ip).get("Runs")
        assert isinstance(runs, int), f"the hazard report counts no runs: {runs!r}"
        before = _link_counters(dut_ip)
        load = _load.Load()
        stop = threading.Event()
        threads = [threading.Thread(target=_gets_until, args=(dut_ip, "/status", n, stop, load), name=f"hazard-get-{n}") for n in range(_ECHO_READERS)]
        try:
            for thread in threads:
                thread.start()
            put = http_client.fetch(dut_ip, 80, "PUT", "/status", {"UartHazards": True}, timeout_s=_REQUEST_BUDGET_S)
            assert put.status_code == 200 and put.json().get("result") == {"UartHazards": "Valid"}, f"PUT /status did not start the hazard run: {put.status_code} {put.body[:120]!r}"
            wait_until(lambda: _hazard_run_ended(dut_ip, runs), timeout_s=_HAZARD_RUN_TIMEOUT_S, poll_interval_s=_WAIT_POLL_S, description="the hazard run's end under the readers' load")
        finally:
            stop.set()
            alive = _load.join(threads, _JOIN_TIMEOUT_S)
        assert not alive, f"{alive} never finished within {_JOIN_TIMEOUT_S:g}s - possible real deadlock under load"

    def run_isolated(self, script_path: "str | Path", *, soft_reset_after: bool = True, timeout_s: "float | None" = None, allow_recovery: bool = True, **extras: object) -> str:

        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_s
        last_exc: BaseException | None = None
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            try:

                    return True
            except Exception as exc:

            time.sleep(min(poll_interval_s, max(deadline - time.monotonic(), 0.0)))

        assert per_call_s > _CAP_BINDING_ANSWER_S, f"the answer window {_CAP_BINDING_ANSWER_S}s must stay under the per-call timeout {per_call_s}s"

        ("WEBSERVER", "W", "HTTP_REFUSED"),
        ("WEBSERVER", "W", "HTTP_PEER_RESET"),
    )
    def test_concurrent_mixed_body_sizes_are_never_answered_with_the_wrong_status(dut_ip: str, request: pytest.FixtureRequest, result_note: "_load.Note") -> None:
        # max_connections bodies can be in flight at once, so the simultaneous contiguous demand is that many buffers - the
        # multi-buffer shape that motivated Part I.6, asserted on what the body cap owns.
        reset_all_error_logs(dut_ip, request.node.name)
        time.sleep(_SLOT_RELEASE_WAIT_S)  # the PUT just made can still hold a slot: _serve() releases it after the close
        cap = _body_cap()
        # Repeated well past the build's ceiling however high it is raised, so the storm overloads admission.
        sizes = [512, cap * 2, cap, _OLD_CONTENT_CAP, 64, cap + 1, 900, cap * 2] * max(_STORM_REPEAT_MIN, _MAX_CONNECTIONS)
        outcomes: dict[str, dict[int, int | str]] = {"answered": {}, "refused": {}, "other": {}}
        lock = threading.Lock()
        threads: list[threading.Thread] = []
        try:
            for i, size in enumerate(sizes):
                thread = threading.Thread(target=_sized_worker, args=(dut_ip, i, size, outcomes, lock), name=f"put-{i}")
                threads.append(thread)
                thread.start()
        finally:
            alive = _load.join(threads, _STORM_JOIN_S)
        assert not alive, f"{len(alive)} worker(s) never finished within {_STORM_JOIN_S:g}s - possible real deadlock under concurrent mixed-body load"
        answered, refused, other = outcomes["answered"], outcomes["refused"], outcomes["other"]
        # Most are refused at the ceiling, its reject-when-full (measured ~25% on 2026-09-22, at every size including 64 B): a refusal

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["escalate", "hold_console"])
    def test_the_supervisor_escalation_reboot_is_attributed(board: "Board", bench: "BenchBridge", dut_ip: str, result_note: "Callable[[str], None]", mode: str) -> None:
        # hold_console: the host holds the port open, reading nothing, while the task keeps dying - still the budget's reboot.
        # The script's log is RAM-only, so escalate reads its entry off the rounds; hold_console prints none, and the
        # entry is pinned by tests/test_asy_system_service.py::test_the_supervisor_escalates_past_the_failure_budget.
        try:
            _evidence(board, bench, dut_ip, f"reset-reason-escalation-{mode}")
            if mode == "hold_console":
                board.run_isolated_expect_reset(DEVICE_SCRIPTS_DIR / "system_service_restarts_a_real_dead_task.py", timeout_s=_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_S, hold_unread_s=3 * _WDT_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000, mode=mode)
            else:
                facts = parse_facts(board.run_isolated_expect_reset(DEVICE_SCRIPTS_DIR / "system_service_restarts_a_real_dead_task.py", timeout_s=_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_S, mode=mode), allow_missing_done=True)
                assert facts.get("mode") == mode and any(key.startswith("round_") for key in facts), f"the escalation reported no round before the reset: {facts}"

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["escalate", "hold_console"])
    def test_the_supervisor_escalation_reboot_is_attributed(board: "Board", bench: "BenchBridge", dut_ip: str, result_note: "Callable[[str], None]", mode: str) -> None:
        # hold_console: the host holds the port open, reading nothing, while the task keeps dying - still the budget's reboot.
        # The script's log is RAM-only, so escalate reads its entry off the rounds; hold_console prints none, and the
        # entry is pinned by tests/test_asy_system_service.py::test_the_supervisor_escalates_past_the_failure_budget.
        try:
            _evidence(board, bench, dut_ip, f"reset-reason-escalation-{mode}")
            if mode == "hold_console":
                board.run_isolated_expect_reset(DEVICE_SCRIPTS_DIR / "system_service_restarts_a_real_dead_task.py", timeout_s=_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_S, hold_unread_s=3 * _WDT_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000, mode=mode)
            else:
                facts = parse_facts(board.run_isolated_expect_reset(DEVICE_SCRIPTS_DIR / "system_service_restarts_a_real_dead_task.py", timeout_s=_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_S, mode=mode), allow_missing_done=True)
                assert facts.get("mode") == mode and any(key.startswith("round_") for key in facts), f"the escalation reported no round before the reset: {facts}"
                assert "starter_calls" not in facts, f"the watch ended without the budget's reboot: {facts}"
                assert _round_holds_the_budget_entry(facts), f"no round before the reset holds SYSTEM's TASK_BUDGET_REBOOT entry: {facts}"

    def test_a_console_interrupt_is_attributed(board: "Board", bench: "BenchBridge", dut_ip: str, result_note: "Callable[[str], None]") -> None:
        # One Ctrl-C on a freshly opened port: the firmware drops to the REPL with its watchdog armed and the watchdog resets.
        try:
            _evidence(board, bench, dut_ip, "reset-reason-console-interrupt")
            with serial.Serial(board.device, 115200, timeout=1.0) as port:

            wait_until(lambda: not board.is_device_present(), timeout_s=_WDT_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000 + _LOSS_MARGIN_S, description="the watchdog reset after a console interrupt")

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["exception", "base"])
    def test_a_loop_ended_by_an_exception_after_boot_is_attributed(board: "Board", bench: "BenchBridge", dut_ip: str, result_note: "Callable[[str], None]", kind: str) -> None:
        # mpremote's Ctrl-C records 21, which the script's boot clears; its loop then ends by an OSError or a SystemExit at the
        # first wait after BOOT_DONE: the entry records 22 and resets the chip at once. Normal boot, no flash write.
        try:
            _evidence(board, bench, dut_ip, f"reset-reason-loop-end-{kind}")
            facts = parse_facts(board.run_isolated_expect_reset(DEVICE_SCRIPTS_DIR / "reset_code_loop_end.py", timeout_s=_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_S, KIND=kind, BOOT_DONE=str(_BOOT_DONE)), allow_missing_done=True)
            # No drop-off wait: the reset is immediate. Its phase fact may be lost in rp2's CDC queue, so only a wrong one
            # fails: 22 alone proves BOOT_DONE, written only then over a record the script's boot cleared (A.7).
            assert facts.get("raised_in_phase", _BOOT_DONE) == _BOOT_DONE, f"{kind}: the loop ended in another phase: {facts}"

isolated_board = <harness.Board object at 0x7fa588b4d0>
result_note = <function result_note.<locals>._note at 0x7fa3f53ce0>

    @pytest.mark.provokes_log(
        "its levels run two past the ceiling, whose refusals trace HTTP_REFUSED",
        ("WEBSERVER", "W", "HTTP_REFUSED"),
        ("WEBSERVER", "W", "HTTP_PEER_RESET"),
    )
    @pytest.mark.ends_unreachable
    def test_serving_sweep_at_the_reactive_default(isolated_board: "Board", dut_ip: str, result_note: "_load.Note") -> None:
        # Ascending levels up past the configured ceiling, on one boot: the realistic case is a running
        # device whose heap carries every earlier burst. The bar is I.4(e): not one allocation failure.
        ceiling = configured_max_connections()
        levels = list(range(4, ceiling + 3, 2))
        tallies: dict[int, dict[str, int]] = {}
        stop = threading.Event()
        driver = threading.Thread(target=sweep_levels, args=(dut_ip, levels, stop, tallies), name="sweep-driver")
        try:
            driver.start()
            output = isolated_board.run_isolated(DEVICE_SCRIPTS / "serving_at_default_gc.py", timeout_s=_SERVING_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_S)
        finally:
            stop.set()
            alive = _load.join([driver], _DRIVER_JOIN_S)
        assert not alive, "the load driver is still running after its own test - it would hammer every test that follows"
        facts = parse_facts(output)
        at = _stage(facts)
        assert facts.get("webserver_built") is True, f"{at}: main() had built no webserver by the end of the boot wait: {facts}"
        assert "phases_incomplete" not in facts, f"{at}: the script never saw a full idle/load/idle cycle: {facts.get('phases_incomplete')}"
        maps = heap_map.parse_labelled(output)
        for label, m in sorted(maps.items()):
            result_note(f"{at}: {label:>7} free={m.free_bytes} largest_free_run={m.largest_free_run} runs={len(m.free_runs)} placeable256={m.placeable(256)} placeable2048={m.placeable(2048)}")
        for n in levels:
            result_note(f"{at}: N={n} (ceiling {ceiling}): {tallies.get(n)}")

    def wait_until(
        check_fn: "Callable[[], bool]",
        timeout_s: float,
        poll_interval_s: float = _WAIT_UNTIL_POLL_S,
        description: str = "condition",
    ) -> bool:
        # Bounded poll-until-condition wait, test-harness-only (never used to change src/'s own real
        # timing - SPECIFICATION.md Part F.3). Polls `check_fn()` until truthy or `timeout_s` elapses,
        # treating a raising check as not-yet-ready; always returns True or raises TimeoutError.
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_s
        last_exc: BaseException | None = None
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            try:
                if check_fn():
                    return True
            except Exception as exc:
                last_exc = exc
            time.sleep(min(poll_interval_s, max(deadline - time.monotonic(), 0.0)))
        try:
            if check_fn():
                return True
        except Exception as exc:
            last_exc = exc
        detail = f" (last error: {last_exc!r})" if last_exc is not None else ""

    @pytest.mark.provokes_log(
        "the storm overloads admission: each refusal traces HTTP_REFUSED (_assert_ceiling_traced)",
        ("WEBSERVER", "W", "HTTP_REFUSED"),
        ("WEBSERVER", "W", "HTTP_PEER_RESET"),
    )
    def test_concurrent_mixed_body_sizes_are_never_answered_with_the_wrong_status(dut_ip: str, request: pytest.FixtureRequest, result_note: "_load.Note") -> None:
        # max_connections bodies can be in flight at once, so the simultaneous contiguous demand is that many buffers - the
        # multi-buffer shape that motivated Part I.6, asserted on what the body cap owns.
        reset_all_error_logs(dut_ip, request.node.name)
        time.sleep(_SLOT_RELEASE_WAIT_S)  # the PUT just made can still hold a slot: _serve() releases it after the close
        cap = _body_cap()
        # Repeated well past the build's ceiling however high it is raised, so the storm overloads admission.
        sizes = [512, cap * 2, cap, _OLD_CONTENT_CAP, 64, cap + 1, 900, cap * 2] * max(_STORM_REPEAT_MIN, _MAX_CONNECTIONS)
        outcomes: dict[str, dict[int, int | str]] = {"answered": {}, "refused": {}, "other": {}}
        lock = threading.Lock()
        threads: list[threading.Thread] = []
        try:
            for i, size in enumerate(sizes):
                thread = threading.Thread(target=_sized_worker, args=(dut_ip, i, size, outcomes, lock), name=f"put-{i}")
                threads.append(thread)
                thread.start()
        finally:
            alive = _load.join(threads, _STORM_JOIN_S)
        assert not alive, f"{len(alive)} worker(s) never finished within {_STORM_JOIN_S:g}s - possible real deadlock under concurrent mixed-body load"
        answered, refused, other = outcomes["answered"], outcomes["refused"], outcomes["other"]
        # Most are refused at the ceiling, its reject-when-full (measured ~25% on 2026-09-22, at every size including 64 B): a refusal
        # is counted, not failed - but ONLY a refusal.

        poll_interval_s: float = _WAIT_UNTIL_POLL_S,
        description: str = "condition",
    ) -> bool:
        # Bounded poll-until-condition wait, test-harness-only (never used to change src/'s own real
        # timing - SPECIFICATION.md Part F.3). Polls `check_fn()` until truthy or `timeout_s` elapses,

        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_s
        last_exc: BaseException | None = None
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            try:
                if check_fn():
                    return True
            except Exception as exc:
                last_exc = exc
            time.sleep(min(poll_interval_s, max(deadline - time.monotonic(), 0.0)))

            if check_fn():

        except Exception as exc:

        detail = f" (last error: {last_exc!r})" if last_exc is not None else ""

    def test_single_core_timing_headroom_holds_under_normal_full_task_load(board: "Board", request: pytest.FixtureRequest) -> None:

## Bench 2026-11-11 06:13:00 UTC - a: 4a red, one host-architecture cause; b-d go on (hardware tiers do not use it)

- 4a (05:53-06:11, 1,090 s, rc 1): scripts/test.sh failed before L3, no hardware touched. Every MicroPython file and all
  48 tests_scripts failures/errors have one cause: `SyntaxError: invalid micropython decorator` at src/crc_checks.py:20,
  `@micropython.viper` (in src/ since snapshot 58, dab692d6; the last 4a on this Pi was 11-05, before it).
- Why: the v1.29.0 Unix port picks its native emitter by host CPU (ports/unix/mpconfigport.h:67-85: x64, x86, thumb,
  arm, rv32); aarch64 has none, so on the bench Pi 4 (arm64) both @micropython.native and @micropython.viper are a
  compile-time SyntaxError. Checked directly on the freshly built build-standard binary (05:42 UTC): a three-line
  @micropython.native function fails the same way. CI's x86_64 runners have the X64 emitter, so CI stays green; the
  rp2 image (thumb) is unaffected (snapshot 58 runs it on silicon).
- Consequence: on this host the unit tier, the twin tier and every tests_scripts twin boot cannot run, and k's two
  chroot legs on this Pi (arm64) will fail the same way at scripts/test.sh. The fix is in the tree, not the bench.
- The hardware tiers (flash, bench) run the board and do not use the Unix port; their runs keep --skip-lower-levels as
  the sheet has them. b, c and d go on as planned. Log: logs/4a.log (from line 151104).
